newsitem.title: USA: Albright presses strong U.S. world role.
newsitem.headline: Albright presses strong U.S. world role.

text.p: Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright, affirming her support for strong and active U.S. diplomacy, promised on Wednesday Washington would play a heightened role to reduce tensions in Cyprus, India-Pakistan and Nagorno-Karabakh.

In testimony prepared for delivery at her Senate confirmation hearing, she also vowed to work as a "tough team" with other senior administration officials to promote a fair world trading system and make the United States a "dynamic hub of the global economy."

Albright, the first woman nominated to the top American diplomatic post, told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee "we must be the authors of the history of our age" and "our leadership must be sustained if our interests are to be protected around the world."

As expected, she made an emphatic pitch to Congress -- which has forced what some consider draconian cuts in foreign affairs spending in recent years -- to restore funding because "we need a first-class diplomacy ... Force alone can be a blunt instrument and there are many problems it cannot solve."

But while stressing that American leadership must be sustained to protect U.S. interests around the world, she also said, "We do not have unlimited resources, nor do we have unlimited responsibilities ... we have to weigh our commitments carefully."

On Cyprus, Albright said "we are prepared to play a heightened role in promoting a resolution" on the divided island. On India and Pakistan, she said "we will again consider the prospects for reducing the tensions" there. On Nagorno-Karabakh, a region of Azerbaijan populated by Armenians where some 15,000 have died in six years of war, she said the United States "is prepared to play a more visible role in helping to arrange a settlement."
